segments.t: Thinking on his feet to salvage the situation, Chef Barinov claims he was purposely holding back his congratulations until tonight so he would not spoil his big birthday surprise. Though skeptical, Elena agrees to wait and see what he has prepared for the evening.
Витя, это фиаско!
Держусь, тебя не поздравляю.
А ты не можешь потерпеть до вечера!
То есть ты подготовил мне сюрприз?
Вот именно, сюрприз!
Просто я не верю.
Обычно у тебя сюрпризы случаются сами собой.
Потом ты просто просишь за них прощения.
Вот увидим вечером!
Спасибо большое, очень приятно.
Я позвоню и отметим.
До вечера, любимая!
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
Витя, это фиаско!
'Vitya, this is a fiasco!' Chef Barinov brings out the contrast between 'proper name' and 'this' in a few short words.
Держусь, тебя не поздравляю.
'I am holding back, not congratulating you.' Chef Barinov brings out the contrast between 'hold back' and 'you' in a few short words.
А ты не можешь потерпеть до вечера!
'And you cannot be patient until evening!' Chef Barinov addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'in the evening'. Elena answers right away.
То есть ты подготовил мне сюрприз?
'So you prepared a surprise for me?' The meaning hinges on 'that' working together with 'surprise' in spoken Russian.
Вот именно, сюрприз!
'Precisely, a surprise!' In Russian, the idea of 'here' flows naturally into 'surprise' without extra filler words.
Просто я не верю.
'I simply do not believe it.' Notice how Russian expresses 'simply' and 'to believe' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Обычно у тебя сюрпризы случаются сами собой.
'Usually your surprises happen by themselves.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'usual' before landing on 'oneself'.
Потом ты просто просишь за них прощения.
'Then you simply ask forgiveness for them.' The meaning hinges on 'then' working together with 'forgiveness' in spoken Russian.
Вот увидим вечером!
'Well we will see tonight!' An emphatic spoken line centered on the verb meaning 'to see'. Elena answers right away.
Спасибо большое, очень приятно.
'Thank you very much, that is very nice.' Elena anchors the line on 'thank you', while 'pleasant' completes the thought.
Я позвоню и отметим.
'I will call and we will celebrate.' The grammar packs 'I' and 'will celebrate' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
До вечера, любимая!
'Until evening, darling!' The meaning hinges on 'until' working together with 'favourite' in spoken Russian. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.

That brings Viktor's narrow escape to a close. Notice how Elena jokes that Viktor's surprises usually happen by accident and end with him asking for forgiveness. See you next time!
Хорошего дня!
